title: Transport vocabulary + prepositions of movement
grammarNote: В английском с разными видами транспорта используются РАЗНЫЕ глаголы и предлоги. Нельзя просто сказать "I go in bus" — нужно "I get on the bus" или "I take the bus". Также предлоги движения (along, across, past, through, towards) передают разные направления движения.

grammarTable.subject: take the bus/train/taxi
grammarTable.example: I always take the number 14 bus to university.

grammarTable.subject: get on / get off
grammarTable.example: Get on at WKU, get off at the city centre.

grammarTable.subject: catch a bus/train
grammarTable.example: Hurry! We'll miss the train if we don't catch it.

grammarTable.subject: miss the bus/train
grammarTable.example: I missed the last bus — I had to take a taxi.

grammarTable.subject: by bus/train/car/plane
grammarTable.example: I travel to Almaty by train. · She came by plane.

grammarTable.subject: on foot / on horseback
grammarTable.example: The university is 20 minutes on foot from here.

grammarTable.subject: drive / ride / fly
grammarTable.example: He drives a car. · She rides a bicycle. · They fly to Astana.

grammarTable.subject: along / across / past
grammarTable.example: Walk along the road. · Run across the park. · Drive past the school.

rows.example: Get on the bus at the first stop. (large vehicle)
Get in the taxi — it's waiting outside! (small vehicle)
Get off at the third stop after the bridge.
Get out of the taxi here — the café is right there.
Walk along the river embankment to reach the park.
Run across the square to catch the bus.
The bus goes past the university at 8:15.
Walk through the underpass to cross the road.
Walk towards the river and you'll see the bridge.
Walk away from the market — the museum is in the opposite direction.

rows.form: take / catch a bus, train, flight
rows.example: I need to catch the 9:15 train to Astana.

rows.form: book / buy a ticket in advance
rows.example: Book your train ticket at least a week in advance.
You have to check in at least 90 minutes before departure.
Boarding for flight 6A402 has now started at Gate B2.
Change trains at Astana and take the express to Almaty.
There's a direct train from Uralsk to Oral — only 20 minutes.
✅ I get on the bus. / I take the bus.
✅ She travels by car. (by + transport!)
✅ Get on the train. (train = large vehicle → on!)
✅ Walk across the bridge. (across = from one side to other)

grammarTip:
Три ключевых правила:
① get ON/OFF = большие транспортные средства: bus, train, plane, metro
② get IN/OUT OF = маленькие: car, taxi
③ by + transport (без артикля!): by bus · by train · by car · by plane
   НО: on foot (не 'by foot'!) · in a taxi (не 'by taxi' в разговорной речи)

Предлоги движения — подсказка:
along = вдоль (длинный путь рядом с чем-то)
across = пересечь (с одной стороны на другую)
past = мимо (не останавливаясь)
through = насквозь (внутри чего-то)

exercises.text: I always ___ the number 7 bus to the city centre.
exercises.hint: take the bus = the standard collocation.

exercises.text: ___ the taxi — the driver is waiting.
exercises.hint: Taxi = small vehicle → get IN the taxi.

exercises.text: I travel to Almaty ___ train — it's the most relaxing way.
exercises.hint: by + transport (no article): by train, by bus, by plane.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct preposition of movement.
exercises.text: Walk ___ the embankment until you reach the bridge.
exercises.hint: Along = moving in a direction following a long object (road, river, embankment).

exercises.text: She ___ the last bus and had to walk home.
exercises.hint: "miss the bus/train" = not catch it in time; arrive too late.

exercises.text: "She travels with car" is correct English.
exercises.hint: "by car" not "with car". Transport uses "by": by car, by bus, by plane.

exercises.text: Get ___ at the third stop — the university is right there.
exercises.hint: Get off = leave the bus/train at your stop.

exercises.text: Walk ___ the park to get to the bus station faster.
exercises.hint: Across = from one side of the park to the other. Crossing an open space.

questions.hint: Train = large vehicle → get ON the train.

questions.text: She travels to Astana ___ plane every month.
What is the correct form for arriving at destination by foot?
questions.hint: "on foot" — this is the fixed expression. (NOT "by foot"!)

questions.text: "___ the road at the zebra crossing."
questions.hint: Cross the road = go from one side to the other.

questions.text: Walk ___ the bridge and turn right — the station is 100m ahead.
questions.hint: Across = from one side to the other (bridge, road, square).

questions.text: She ___ the 8:15 train because she woke up late.
questions.hint: miss the train = fail to catch it; arrive too late.
Taxi = small vehicle → Get IN the taxi.

questions.text: "Walk ___ the market — the museum is in the other direction."
questions.hint: "away from" = moving in the opposite direction from something.

questions.text: "Walk ___ the tunnel to reach the other side of the road."
questions.hint: "through" = moving inside an enclosed space (tunnel, forest, building).

questions.text: You need to ___ trains at Astana — there's no direct service.
questions.hint: "change trains at..." = transfer to a different train.
"ride" is used for bicycles, motorbikes, and horses — not buses or trains.

questions.text: "By bus, by car, by plane" all follow the same pattern.
questions.hint: "by + transport" — same pattern for all vehicles (no article after "by").

questions.text: "Walk ___ the park — it's a beautiful shortcut."
questions.hint: "through" = moving inside an enclosed or defined space (park, forest, tunnel).

questions.text: Get ___ the bus here — the WKU stop is only two stops away.
questions.hint: Get on = board a large vehicle (bus, train).

questions.text: To say you took an aeroplane, you say...
questions.hint: "fly" is the verb for air travel. I flew to Almaty. She flies every week.
